name: british-thriller-trailer-braams
style: British crime-drama trailer tension, UK television thriller, English voices spoken not sung. Ticking clock pulse, a rising synth riser climbing under urgent London shouting. One colossal low brass braam with sub drop, a wall of sound. Then a shrill, nasal, plummy English aristocrat in a petulant tantrum, muffled behind car glass. Second riser into a single flatline tone, then dead silence. 14 seconds.
exclude: American accent, US accent, Hollywood, epic orchestra, choir, singing, sung chorus, melodic vocal, rap, cheerful, comedy, trailer voiceover, fade out
lyrics:
[Intro: ticking clock pulse, riser climbing, siren in the rain]
[Spoken, shouted: Essex woman, paramedic, frantic]
Sixty over thirty! Fucking hurry up, we're gonna lose him!
[Spoken, shouted: Cockney man, paramedic, breathless]
Sats dropping, he's peri-arrest!
[Spoken, roared: Cockney driver, raging at traffic]
Two minutes out! Get the fuck out of the way!
[Huge braam, sub drop, everything stops]
[Spoken: Cockney man, disbelief]
Why have we stopped?!
[Spoken, muffled through glass: shrill nasal posh English aristocrat, tantrum, loud]
I said raspberry-shaped hors d'oeuvres!
[Second riser climbing, heart monitor beeping]
[Spoken, quiet: Essex woman, barely a whisper]
Fifty over twen—
[Flatline tone, final hit]
[Silence]
[End]
